quizzes.stem: A handler adds up the output token count of every `message_delta` it receives and reports three times the real cost. What does the page say it should do instead?

options.a: Overwrite the earlier figure, since each event restates the running tally
options.b: Take the input count from the final event and the output count from the first
options.c: Sum them all and then subtract the figure that the opening event gave
options.d: Drop the field and measure the pieces of text that arrived in the stream

explanation.a: The page says "The output count in message_delta is cumulative: replace the stored one, do not add to it".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "the output count comes from the last message_delta" and the input count from `message_start`.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the page says "do not add to it".
explanation.d: Ruled out because usage is read from the events: "Input tokens come from message_start".

quizzes.stem: A stream stops after a content block and the connection closes with no `message_stop` event. What should the assembler return?

options.a: A message whose stop reason is `end_turn`
options.b: The text it has, marked as a short answer
options.c: An error that says the message is incomplete
options.d: A blank message so that the caller can try again

explanation.c: The page says a stream like that "is an incomplete message, not a short one".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the same sentence says "an incomplete message, not a short one".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "the stop reason arrives in message_delta, near the end, so a cut stream has none".
explanation.d: Ruled out because accepting it hides the loss: "Raise, so that the caller can decide".

quizzes.stem: A client prints text as it arrives. Midway, an `error` event with `overloaded_error` appears although the HTTP status was 200. What is the right handling?

options.a: Keep the partial text as the final answer and finish the turn without more work
options.b: Treat the call as failed, drop the partial output and send the whole request again
options.c: Ignore the event, since the status line already reported that the call went well
options.d: Resume the stream from the last received byte once the service has recovered

explanation.b: The page says "discard the partial output first and retry the whole request".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the partial text is the loss: "the user may already have read the partial text" and the answer is cut short, so it is not final.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "A status check alone cannot tell you a stream succeeded".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a stream that failed midway "cannot be resumed from the last byte".

quizzes.stem: A team streams a long report only because they believe it lowers the bill. According to the page, what is the better reason to stream?

options.a: A tool input that is valid at every fragment
options.b: A lower price for each of the output tokens
options.c: An exemption from the limits that apply to other calls
options.d: A lengthy reply that a person is waiting to read

explanation.d: The page's first case is "A person is waiting for a long answer".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Streaming changes when the bytes arrive, not what the tokens cost".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Streamed calls count against the same limits as the others".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "the fragment is not an object, and the object that comes is not final until the block ends".

quizzes.stem: A support app shows a streamed reply that includes a tool call. When may it run the tool?

options.a: After the block holding it has stopped and its joined fragments have parsed
options.b: As soon as the tool name appears in the opening event of the block
options.c: Whenever the first fragment turns out to be a complete object
options.d: Before the text, because tool blocks are always listed in front

explanation.a: The page says "do not act on a tool call until its block has stopped and its input has parsed".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "The input is incomplete until the block stops".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a fragment is not an object: "the fragment is not an object, and the object that comes is not final until the block ends".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "content lists the blocks in index order", not by kind.

quizzes.stem: Which pair of behaviours does a correct assembler show for an unrecognised event type and for a stream that ends early?

options.a: It skips both and returns the content it holds
options.b: It raises on the first and returns what the second gave
options.c: It skips the first and raises on the second
options.d: It raises on both so that nothing is guessed

explanation.c: The page says to "ignore event types you do not know" and that a stream without `message_stop` "is an incomplete message, not a short one".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the first is skipped "because the API may add new ones".
explanation.a: Ruled out because a cut stream "is an incomplete message, not a short one".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the first is skipped: "ignore event types you do not know".

quizzes.stem: A job generates a thirty-minute report behind a proxy that cuts idle connections. Why does streaming help?

options.a: The output limit rises, so the report fits in a single answer
options.b: Steady events keep the link active, so no timer ever expires
options.c: The proxy is avoided by sending the events through another port
options.d: The output is compressed, so it crosses the proxy faster

explanation.b: The page says "Events keep arriving, so a proxy never sees an idle connection".
explanation.a: Ruled out because streaming changes when the bytes arrive "or what the limits allow".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a stream is "the same POST request to the same URL".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Streaming changes when the bytes arrive", and it does not change the size of what arrives.

quizzes.stem: A stream holds a thinking block, a text block and a tool block. In which order does an assembler list them?

options.a: By how many fragments each one received
options.b: By the moment at which each one finished
options.c: With thinking first, text next and tools last
options.d: By the index that the events give each one

explanation.d: The page says "content lists the blocks in index order".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the order is "not in the order they stopped".
explanation.c: Ruled out because blocks are "never sorted by type or by size".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the order is fixed by the index: "content lists the blocks in index order".
